fatal_errors: Fails to identify the specific AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy and its FCC+B2 as-cast microstructure.
Misstates the relevant condition as ultralow temperature rather than intermediate-temperature aging near 550–750°C.
Treats the transition itself as an intervention instead of specifying thermal aging at approximately 600°C and 750°C.
Predicts only a ductile-to-brittle transition rather than the required non-monotonic ductile–brittle–ductile response.
Omits the central L12 ordering, jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary morphology, planar slip, stress concentration, and ductile transition-zone mechanisms.
The cited evidence concerns tungsten single crystals and does not support the proposed behavior in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed falsification experiment is not an operational or discriminating measurement.
explanation: The hypothesis only recognizes that a high-entropy alloy might show a ductility transition and generically invokes dislocation motion. It does not reconstruct the material, aging treatment, temperature window, structural mediators, or recovery mechanism. Its ultralow-temperature rationale is a different phenomenon derived from evidence about tungsten single crystals. It also fails to predict the essential recovery of ductility at 750°C or propose measurements capable of distinguishing phase-boundary/order-driven embrittlement from conventional impurity-segregation temper embrittlement.
